name: Raghunayaka Perumal Temple (Ammaji Mandir), Ayodhya
deity: Vishnu as Rama, worshipped as Raghunayaka (Chakravarthi Thirumagan), with Sita Piratti — the Sri Vaishnava Divya Desam worship at the Ammaji Mandir
period: A Divya Desam of Vada Nadu, sung by five Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: In Ayodhya, the city of Rama, the Sri Vaishnava tradition honours Raghunayaka, the Chakravarthi Thirumagan sung by five Alvars — a Vada Nadu Divya Desam, worshipped at the Ammaji Mandir.

sections.history: Thiru Ayodhi, Ayodhya, is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu praised by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Vada Nadu, the northern region of the tradition. Thirteen verses sing its lord: six by Periyalvar, four by Kulasekara Alvar, and one each by Nammalvar, Thondaradippodi Alvar and Thirumangai Alvar. For South Indian pilgrims in the Sri Vaishnava tradition, worship of the Divya Desam lord is offered at the Ammaji Mandir. It was founded in 1904 by Yogi Parthasarathy Iyengar, and after his death his wife, Yogi Singammal, called Ammaji, completed it and organised its daily worship and festivals, which gave the temple the name by which it is known. The Alvars' verses, not any one building, are the oldest witness to this Divya Desam.
sections.architecture: The Ammaji Mandir is built in the Dravidian style, a South Indian temple in the north, and the Pushkala Vimana is named as the vimana of this Divya Desam. Its sacred water, the theertham, is the river Sarayu. The temple holds images of Rama, Sita and Ranganatha, along with a processional image linked to the Divya Desam of Darbhasayanam at Thiruppullani in Tamil Nadu. Shrines of Nammalvar, Thirumangai Alvar, Ramanuja (Udayavar) and Manavala Mamunigal stand within, gathering the Sri Vaishnava lineage under one roof.
sections.legends: Ayodhya is held by tradition to be the capital of Rama and the Ikshvaku kings, and the city where the Ramayana unfolds. The Alvars sang it as the home of the lord they call Raghunayaka and Chakravarthi Thirumagan, the son of the emperor Dasharatha. Periyalvar, who sang six of its thirteen verses, and Kulasekara Alvar, who sang four, loved Rama with a particular tenderness. The Sarayu, flowing by the city, is the river of its tradition, and pilgrims bathe in it with devotion.
sections.festivals: The principal festival is Sri Rama Navami, celebrated at the Ammaji Mandir as a utsavam over five days with worship and processions. The Sri Vaishnava calendar's festivals, among them Vaikunta Ekadashi and the days of the Alvars and acharyas, are observed as at other Divya Desams. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: A quiet corner of devotion for the Sri Vaishnava pilgrim, where Tamil verses of the Alvars are remembered beside the Sarayu in the heart of the north. Sit before the images of Rama, Sita and Ranganatha, then visit the shrines of the Alvars and acharyas. Arrive in the morning, when the city is calmer, and keep time for a walk to the river.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Rama Navami and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Ayodhya is in Uttar Pradesh on the Sarayu, with its own railway station and road links to Lucknow and Gorakhpur; the airport at Ayodhya serves the city. The Ammaji Mandir lies within the city; ask locally for the temple of the South Indian Sri Vaishnava tradition.
